Quote supports EXC-002 with setup T_slv, hold not checked.
Quote supports EXC-004 with (N-1) x T_mst.
Quote states limits follow project defaults; implementation constraint, check none.
EXC-006 forbids these commands between the clocks; MUST_NOT correct.
Documentation/open-item action for the author, not a design behaviour to verify.

Ordering requirement is stated and is a multi-cycle CDC property exercised by scenario, but the actor is the bridge (system), not a signal-level assertion. Check scenario is right; the actor should be system.
Quote is a rationale for using -ignore_clock_latency; the normative constraint is already in EXC-001 to EXC-005. Also lists the alternative -datapath_only for Vivado, so 'shall' is not stated.
Quote cites REQ-TIM-003 requiring post-CTS latency difference below the guard band; it is a timing signoff check.

duplicates.reason: Both require the launch flop and first synchronizer stage to be adjacent; 17.2-01 has the stronger 'shall' wording.

questions.question: Placement adjacency is 'should' in 17.1.2 but 'shall' in 17.2. Which strength applies?

EXC-001 gives (N-1) x T_slv, but 'the same two commands' are used for EXC-002 to EXC-005. Does hold check really get disabled with set_false_path -hold, and what are the values of N and T for the 20 ns and 10 ns examples?
The guard band is 'one destination period' and the post-CTS latency difference limit is tied to it. Which destination clock applies in each direction?
